title_prefix: One stall round disconnects a peer: the
mechanism: retry-timed-out-requests (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1283-1320) iterates every timed-out in-flight HASH and calls record-block-timeout (src/networking/peer.lisp:1549-1553) once per hash, incrementing one per-peer counter that disconnects at +max-block-timeouts+ = 15 (src/networking/peer.lisp:1465). The per-peer in-flight cap is 16 (ibd-context max-in-flight, src/networking/ibd.lisp:171), and request-blocks-from-peers tops a peer up to that cap in a single call, so a peer that goes silent has 16 requests of nearly the same age: they all cross the threshold in the same pass and the counter goes 0 -> 16 in ONE call. The counter is only ever reset by record-block-received-from-peer (src/networking/peer.lisp:1555-1563), i.e. by an actual delivery. The timeout itself is compute-block-download-timeout = 90 + 5*(n-1) seconds (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1217-1236), stamped once per start-ibd from the peer count (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1923), and request-blocks-from-peers substitutes a flat +block-stalling-timeout+ = 30 s whenever the validated tip is within +stalling-near-tip-margin+ = 144 blocks of the header tip OR the block queue is saturated (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1366-1372). Core has two separate rules and neither has this shape: the block-download timeout (refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:6109-6122) is one decision per PEER, taken on the front in-flight block, against state.m_downloading_since + nPowTargetSpacing * (1 + 0.5 * other_downloading_peers) -- and m_downloading_since is re-stamped every time the FRONT block is delivered (:1223) and set when the peer's list goes from empty to non-empty (:1263), so the clock measures SILENCE since the last delivery, not request age; the stalling rule (:6094-6107) fires only when state.m_stalling_since is set, i.e. when the download window cannot move at all, and it doubles its own timeout from BLOCK_STALLING_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 2 s toward BLOCK_STALLING_TIMEOUT_MAX 64 s after each use precisely so our own bandwidth cannot mass-evict peers. We have no analogue of m_stalling_since (grep: nothing in ibd.lisp) and no back-off.
consequence: The exact disconnect rule is: a :ready peer holding N in-flight blocks that delivers nothing is disconnected after ceiling(15/N) retry passes -- executed: N=16 or 15 -> 1 pass, N=8 -> 2, N=4 -> 4, N=2 -> 8, N=1 -> 15. With a full 16-block window that is one stall round: 125 seconds of silence during bulk download with 8 peers, or 30 seconds whenever we are within 144 blocks of the header tip or the queue is saturated. Core's floor for the same peer is 600 seconds with one downloading peer and 2700 seconds with eight, measured from the last delivery. So a peer on a slow or lossy link whose first delivery of a freshly issued 16-block batch arrives later than the timeout is dropped before that delivery can reset the counter -- executed: 16 requests aged 126 s against a 125 s timeout leave the peer :DISCONNECTED, and the delivery that follows resets the counter to 0 on an already-disconnected peer. The 15-timeout budget whose own docstring says it exists to 'tolerate a normal stalled batch without evicting peers who are simply mid-transit on big blocks' is therefore spent by a single round. The near-tip branch is not an edge case: any node 16 to 144 blocks behind (a restart after a short outage, ordinary catch-up) satisfies both the 30-second timeout and a full 16-block window at once. Each drop then feeds the refill loop of 33c6687d. S2 and not S1: honest peers are dropped at a rate that costs eclipse resistance and re-download bandwidth, but the download does not wedge -- the released hashes are re-requested from other peers.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-p2p-s2, warm image, probe file ga11-probe/p2p.lisp. (a) Reproduced: a fresh ibd-context with 16 in-flight blocks from one :ready peer, all backdated 200 s, request-timeout 125, one retry-timed-out-requests call -> (:PER-PEER-IN-FLIGHT-CAP 16 :MAX-BLOCK-TIMEOUTS 15 :REQUEST-TIMEOUT-USED 125 :ROUNDS ((:ROUND 1 :COUNT 16 :STATE :DISCONNECTED))). (b) The exact condition, swept: (:IN-FLIGHT 1 :ROUNDS-TO-DISCONNECT 15) (2 . 8) (4 . 4) (8 . 2) (15 . 1) (16 . 1). (c) The timeouts, read from the image: compute-block-download-timeout 8 = 125, of 1 = 90, +block-stalling-timeout+ = 30, +stalling-near-tip-margin+ = 144, +max-block-timeouts+ = 15, +max-block-request-timeouts+ = 5; Core's counterparts computed from the same constants: 600 s at one downloading peer, 2700 s at eight. (d) Honest-slow peer: 16 requests all aged 126 s with a 125 s timeout -> (:AFTER-RETRY-PASS (:COUNT 16 :STATE :DISCONNECTED)), then record-block-received-from-peer -> count 0 but state still :DISCONNECTED. (e) Drive-site check: request-blocks-from-peers is the only caller that passes PEERS (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1372), it is called from run-ibd's download loop (:2131, :2156) and it is the only place the near-tip/queue-saturated short timeout is chosen (:1366-1372). (f) Core read at refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:133-135 (BLOCK_STALLING_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 2s / _MAX 64s), :147-150 (BASE 1, PER_PEER 0.5), :1218-1224 and :1258-1266 (m_downloading_since set and re-stamped), :6094-6122 (both rules).
fix_shape: Port Core's two rules separately and stop letting the per-hash retry drive the disconnect. Give each peer an m_downloading_since stamp set when its in-flight list goes from empty to non-empty and re-stamped whenever its FRONT in-flight block is delivered (net_processing.cpp:1223, :1263), and disconnect once now > that stamp + nPowTargetSpacing * (BLOCK_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_BASE + BLOCK_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_PER_PEER * other_downloading_peers) -- one decision per peer, on the front block only (:6109-6122). Add the stalling rule with Core's gate: set a per-peer stalling stamp only when the download window cannot move (nothing left to ask this peer for below the window), disconnect after the current stalling timeout, and then DOUBLE that timeout from 2 s toward a 64 s ceiling so our own downstream saturation cannot evict several peers in a row (:6094-6107); a delivery clears the stamp. Keep retry-timed-out-requests as the re-routing mechanism it is -- releasing a hash to another peer after a shorter timeout is useful and should stay -- but drop record-block-timeout and +max-block-timeouts+ from that path entirely, so re-routing never counts toward eviction. A regression test must assert that a peer holding a full window and silent for two minutes survives, and that one silent for the full Core deadline does not.
